sentences.text:
The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Nirsa P.S. Case No.217 of 2021
registered under Sections 147/148/149/353/379/186/413/414/420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860,
Sections 4/21 of Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act, 1957, Rules 4/54 of
Jharkhand Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 2004 and Rule 13 of Jharkhand Minerals (Prevention
of Illegal Mining, Transportation & Storage) Rules, 2017.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.

The petitioner is neither concerned with the seized vehicles nor with the sand allegedly stored near the bank of 'Barakar'
river.

The petitioner and other named accused persons have been implicated in this case by the informant-Mines Inspector, District Minining Office, Dhanbad on the ground that the informant Bablu Singh @ Birendra Singh @ Birendra ... vs The State Of Jharkhand .......... entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 allegedly heard them calling each other by their names.
Except the said fact, there is no other cogent material to connect the petitioner with the alleged offence.

Similarly situated co-accused-Rajendra Singh has already been granted anticipatory bail by a Bench of this Court vide order dated 9 th April,
2024 passed in A.B.A. No.3380 of 2023.
He, however, undertakes to co-operate in the ongoing investigation.
Hence, he may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

3. Learned Spl. P.P. though opposes the petitioner's prayer for grant of anticipatory bail, however,
while responding to the query made by this Court vide order dated 29th October, 2024 regarding criminal antecedent of the petitioner submits that though one more criminal case is pending against him, however, not for the offences under the provisions of Mines and Minerals (Development &
Regulation) Act, 1957, Jharkhand Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 2004 and Jharkhand Minerals (Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation & Storage) Rules, 2017.

entities.text: Jharkhand Minerals (Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation & Storage) Rules, 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on consideration of the materials available on record, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on anticipatory bail.

5. Accordingly, the petitioner, above named, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the court below within three weeks from today, shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Dhanbad in connection with Nirsa P.S. Case No.217 of 2021, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
